claims.text: The initial alloy is a powder-metallurgy-processed WMoTaNbV refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has no pre-existing protective oxide scale.
Pack aluminization at approximately 1000–1100 °C for several hours promotes uniform aluminum diffusion to the alloy surface.
Optimized pack aluminization will produce a continuous Al2O3 scale on WMoTaNbV.
The Al2O3 scale produced by pack aluminization will be dense.
The Al2O3 scale produced by pack aluminization will be adherent.
Aluminum introduced by pack aluminization diffuses to the alloy surface.
Surface aluminum reacts with oxygen to form Al2O3.
The Al2O3 scale acts as a barrier that slows oxygen penetration.
Slower oxygen penetration reduces oxidation kinetics relative to untreated WMoTaNbV.
After 50 hours at 1200 °C in ambient air, aluminized WMoTaNbV will have a significantly thinner oxide scale than untreated WMoTaNbV.
After 50 hours at 1200 °C in ambient air, aluminized WMoTaNbV will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain than untreated WMoTaNbV.
Reduced oxide thickness and oxidation weight gain will enhance structural integrity during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Untreated WMoTaNbV forms a less uniform oxide scale under the specified oxidation conditions.
Untreated WMoTaNbV forms a thicker oxide scale under the specified oxidation conditions.
The untreated alloy degrades faster than the aluminized alloy under the specified oxidation conditions.
The protective effect may not persist at significantly higher temperatures or in other atmospheres without further adaptation.
